Who to watch

Brown leaders (2026)

  • Passing Yards: #15 James Murphy — 114/180, 1,237 YDS, 7 INT
  • Rushing Yards: #2 Matt Childs — 68 CAR, 279 YDS, 4 TD
  • Receiving Yards: #2 Matt Childs — 28 REC, 345 YDS
  • Sacks: #0 Ike Odimegwu — 2.5
  • Tackles: #10 Max Malo — 69

The story: Brown's defense allows 13.2 points a game, second in the Ivy League, and its two senior linebackers (#10 Max Malo, #32 Stefano Montella) are among the six leading tacklers in all of FCS. The offense has scored 15 a game with one touchdown pass all season and 11 turnovers in five games. Captains: #0 Odimegwu, #10 Malo, #15 Murphy, plus Dunn and Thompson.

Cornell leaders (2026)

  • Passing Yards: #8 Garrett Bass-Sulpizio — 94/157, 1,087 YDS, 6 TD, 5 INT
  • Rushing Yards: #41 Jordan Triplett — 56 CAR, 271 YDS, 4 TD
  • Receiving Yards: #80 Brendan Lee — 18 REC, 265 YDS, 1 TD
  • Sacks: #97 Saeed Moghaddam -Adames — 2.5
  • Tackles: #8 Tommy MacPherson — 37

The story: Cornell has the Ivy League's top scoring offense (31.4 a game, 401 yards), just beat then-No. 4 Lehigh 48-38 (its first win over a top-five team since 1939), and has won five of its last six one-possession games. Second-year head coach Dan Swanstrom; preseason All-American tight end #86 Ryder Kurtz.

Ike Odimegwu

DL
6-3 · 240 lbs · Senior
Coppell, Texas (Coppell)
  • FCS Football Central Preseason All-America Second Team (Defense) (preseason).
  • Stats Perform FCS Preseason All-America Third Team (Defense) (preseason).
  • 2025 Second Team All-Ivy (Defense) (DL, ivyleague.com).
2026 so far
  • Defense: 15 tackles (7 solo), 2.5 sacks
2025
  • Defense: 22 tackles (16 solo), 9 sacks, 1 FF
From the press

At Coppell High School in Texas, Odimegwu played both running back and defensive end; as a senior he scooped up a fumbled snap on a Hebron extra-point try and ran it back for two points in a 43-35 Heroes Night win. His Brown bio credits him with the 2022 District 6A Defensive MVP award and first-team all-area honors.

  • As a senior defensive end for Coppell High School on Heroes Night (Coppell 43, Hebron 35), he recovered a fumbled snap on a Hebron point-after attempt and returned it for two points; quoted afterward: "I wanted to be in the endzone." (The Sidekick / Coppell Student Media, Oct. 22, 2022)
  • Earlier in his Coppell career he lined up at running back, opening the scoring with a two-yard touchdown run in a homecoming win over the Wildcats. (The Sidekick / Coppell Student Media (game story, year not shown in index))
  • Named 2022 District 6A Defensive MVP and first-team all-area as a senior at Coppell, per his Brown roster bio. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2025)

From the press

A Santa Cruz High product, Brown led the Bears with nine rushing touchdowns in 2024 and ran for 233 yards and five scores in 2025. He opened last season with two touchdowns against Georgetown, one of them a 49-yard run.

  • In Brown's 46-0 season-opening win over Georgetown on Sept. 20, 2025, he rushed nine times for 69 yards and two touchdowns, including a 49-yard scoring run late in the second quarter. (CBS Sports / AP, Sept. 20, 2025)
  • Appeared in all 10 games in 2025 and ranked second on the team with 233 rushing yards and five touchdowns; in 2024 he led the Bears with nine rushing touchdowns on 33 carries. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2026)
  • As a Santa Cruz High running back he ran for 99 yards and a touchdown in a non-league win over Scotts Valley. (The Pajaronian (Watsonville, Calif.), c. 2021)

From the press

Childs was the 2024 Ivy League Rookie of the Year, leading Brown in rushing and scrimmage yards as a freshman, and followed it with a Second Team All-Ivy season in 2025 (517 rushing yards, eight touchdowns). At Milton Academy he was an All-NEPSAC pick and two-time ISL All-Star.

  • Named 2024 Ivy League Rookie of the Year: in nine games he led Brown in rushing and scrimmage yards with 361 rushing yards, 384 receiving yards and four total touchdowns, including a season-high 101 receiving yards and a touchdown against Harvard. (Ivy League release, Nov. 26, 2024)
  • Earned Ivy League Rookie of the Week honors in back-to-back weeks in October 2024. (Milton Academy news, 2024)
  • Named to Phil Steele's Freshman All-America fourth team after the 2024 season. (Brown Athletics news release, Dec. 20, 2024 (via search index))
  • At Milton Academy (class of 2024) he was an All-NEPSAC selection and two-time Independent School League All-Star; coach Mike Mason called him one of the best athletes he has coached. (Milton Academy news, 2024)
  • In 2025 he ran 137 times for 517 yards and eight touchdowns (ESPN) and earned Second Team All-Ivy League honors (WJAR Turn to 10). (ESPN player page; WJAR Turn to 10, 2025-26)

From the press

Bennett left Windermere Prep in Orlando holding 12 school records, among them 39 career touchdowns, and once scored seven times in a single game as a sophomore. His father played college football at Shepherd University; last season Bennett appeared in all 10 Brown games.

  • As a sophomore at Windermere Prep he scored seven touchdowns (four receiving, three rushing) against Trinity Prep on senior night, a school-record 42 points by one player; he also returned the season-opening kickoff for a touchdown and had early recruiting interest from North Carolina. (Spectrum News 13 (Orlando), Oct. 29, 2020)
  • In Week 2 of 2022 he ran for 249 yards on 13 carries with three touchdowns, the second-highest single-game rushing total in Windermere Prep history. (West Orange Times & Observer, Sept. 5, 2022)
  • Graduated as Windermere Prep's record holder in 12 statistical categories, including total yards (3,198), career rushing yards (2,351), career points (244) and total touchdowns (39); also played lacrosse. His father played college football at Shepherd University. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2026)
  • Appeared in all 10 games for Brown in 2025, rushing 42 times for 161 yards and a touchdown. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2026)

High school: Two-time football captain (2022, 2023) with three varsity letters. Won the California Division 4 State Championship in 2023. Also played lacrosse as an attackman, earning two varsity letters, was named league MVP in 2023, and served as captain in both 2023 and 2024.

Personal: Full name Thomas Knight Ducker. Son of Johanna Kroenlein and Keith Ducker, and has one brother and two sisters. Both parents competed in athletics at Princeton (Keith in football, Johanna in women's lacrosse). His brother, Gavin, plays baseball at William and Mary.

From the press

Ducker anchored the Palma High defense that brought Monterey County its first state football title in 2023, earning all-league honors on both sides of the ball and in lacrosse. He cracked Cornell's rotation as a true freshman, with the Monterey Herald noting a sack against Princeton in 2024. Ivy football runs in the family: his father played football and his mother lacrosse at Princeton.

  • As a true freshman in 2024 he played in four straight Cornell games, recording a sack against Princeton and totaling seven tackles and two sacks for 12 yards in losses. (Monterey Herald, 'Clipboard' column, Nov. 11, 2024 (reposted))
  • Anchored the 2023 Palma defense that won Monterey County's first-ever state football title; earned all-Gabilan Division honors on both offense and defense and was an all-league lacrosse player. (Monterey Herald, Nov. 11, 2024)
  • Family of Princeton athletes: his father played football and his mother lacrosse for the Tigers; brother Gavin plays baseball at William & Mary. (Monterey Herald, Nov. 11, 2024)

The series: Brown vs. Cornell

All-time: Brown leads 39-32-1. First meeting Nov. 16, 1895 (Cornell 6-4). Brown's longest run was nine straight wins, 2008-2016; Cornell then won three in a row (2017-19). The last two years split: Brown 23-21 in Providence in 2024, Cornell 30-24 in double overtime in Ithaca in 2025. Five of the last six were decided by one possession.

Last year, Oct. 25, 2025 at Schoellkopf Field — Cornell 30, Brown 24 (2OT). Brown led 17-6 entering the fourth quarter. Bass-Sulpizio's 10-yard run and McAuliffe's two-point catch made it 17-14 with 3:44 left; Roost's 25-yard field goal with 46 seconds left tied it. In the first overtime Murphy found Pezza from 25 yards, Triplett answered from 2. In the second, Triplett's 1-yard run (his third TD) made it 30-24 and Brown, at the Cornell 5, was stopped on fourth down. Murphy threw for 471 yards; Pezza had 9 catches for 172. Both teams gained exactly 503 yards.

Cornell scores: 1st Jordan Triplett 5 yd run (kick failed, 6-0); 4th Garrett Bass-Sulpizio 10 yd run, John McAuliffe 2-pt pass (17-14); 4th 0:46 Jonathan Roost 25 yd field goal (17-17); OT Triplett 2 yd run, Roost kick (24-24); 2OT Triplett 1 yd run, 2-pt failed (30-24).
Brown scores: 1st Ty Pezza 10 yd pass from James Murphy, Drew Crabtree kick (7-6); 2nd Crabtree 38 yd field goal (10-6); 4th Qwentin Brown 1 yd run, Crabtree kick (17-6); OT Pezza 25 yd pass from Murphy, Crabtree kick (24-17). Source: Cornell Athletics game story, Oct. 25, 2025.

Game day at Brown Stadium

The stadium

Richard Gouse Field at Brown Stadium opened October 24, 1925 — exactly 101 years ago today — before 27,000 at the dedication. Capacity 20,000; the record crowd was 33,000 (Colgate, Thanksgiving 1932, with portable bleachers). FieldTurf since 2021, named for donor Richard I. Gouse '68. First night game: Sept. 25, 2010, Brown 29, Harvard 14. Ivy championship teams: 1976, 1999, 2005, 2008.

Today

  • Family Weekend: pennants to the first 500 fans at Bruno's Backyard.
  • The 1976 Ivy League championship team is recognized at the end of the first quarter (its 50th anniversary).
  • Lot A passes are sold out: arrive early, street parking or campus shuttles.
  • Streaming on ESPN+.

Sources & notes

Built Saturday morning, Oct. 24, 2026, for offline reading. Rosters: brownbears.com (Brown numbers, heights, hometowns, high schools, majors, captains) and cornellbigred.com (Cornell list, bios). Brown photos, 2026 and 2025 statistics, schedules, standings, team stats, head coaches, the betting line and the weather icon: ESPN's public college-football data (site.api.espn.com), pulled Saturday morning. Game preview facts: Brown Athletics game notes (Oct. 22) via BVM Sports; Cornell season outlook (cornellbigred.com, Sept. 14); Cornell's Oct. 25, 2025 game story. Series history: Winsipedia. Stadium: Wikipedia. Forecast: Open-Meteo for 02906.

Caveats: ESPN's roster and the schools' rosters differ in a few places (three Brown players appear only on ESPN's list and are marked; some Cornell numbers may have changed). Cornell's photos come from the school's content network; the few Brown players without an ESPN photo show initials. Statistics are through last weekend's games. Brown's site does not expose bio text to this tool, so Brown bios are built from the official roster line, ESPN statistics, the game notes, and a press search per player (each line names its source; nothing from social media or login-walled sites). Numbers from unverified sources were left out.
